page.layout: One column of running text, set in full width. Below the last line, at the right, the catchword. Head: running title and page number. No marginal notes. A small printer's ornament sits below the text (not transcribed). The strip at the right edge is the neighbouring page (not transcribed).

main_text.p: ufus veniret, exquireret: qui-que civilibus ac privatis ne-gotijs pro sua prudētia præ-essent. Eorum nanque posi-tam quatuor in rebus facul-tatem fuisse reperio: ut iudi-ciorum formulis præesent: privatis in actionibus, veluti pactionibus & testamentis, iis à quibus consulerentur ca-verent: legum, si quæ forté interdum obscuriores vide-rentur, itemque pactionum & testamentorum sententiā interpretarentur: postremo, ut qua de re neque a legibus, neque a privatis cautum est, ipsi quid æquū bonumq; videretur, responderent. ut

page.notes: The words "ut" and "non" are printed on the last line and the catchword. The printed text on the last line is "ut", followed by the catchword "non" alone at the lower right. The text "pactionibus & testamentis" is set in italic in the source; the italic was preserved. Several "s" letters are rendered as "f" in the printed face and were normalised to plain s per the long-s rule (e.g. "fuisse", "consulerentur", "posi-tam"). "fi" was read as "si". "quæ forté" is read as printed, with the acute accent on forté as shown. Some uncertainty in "ut iudi-ciorum" (possible space between ut and iudi). Printed page number "2o" read as 20. The ornament below the text is not text.
